summary: Streaming very large three-dimensional geospatial data by tile, and the only thing on this map that solves that problem in a ratified document. Two facts about its standing are easy to get wrong. It is an OGC Community Standard, not an OGC Implementation Standard, submitted by a single company and approved on that basis; and it was approved 2022-12-17 and published 2023-01-12, not in 2025. Its document address lives under the community-standard path, and the implementation-standard path returns nothing. What it actually specifies is a tree of tiles with an error measure and a refinement rule, a coordinate reference frame, structured metadata and a small styling language. What it deliberately does not specify is the model itself: since version 1.1 the tile payload is the common asset format, and its own four original tile formats are deprecated. Two traps. Its up axis is not the same as that format's, so a transform is applied on every tile. And its security section reads, in full, that no security considerations have been made.

coverage.note: This is the whole point of the standard, and it says so in its own abstract.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, Abstract
sources.quote: This document describes the specification for 3D Tiles, an open standard for streaming massive heterogeneous 3D geospatial datasets.

coverage.note: Each tile carries an error measured in metres, and a rule saying whether children replace the parent or add to it. That pair is what lets a client decide what to draw and what to fetch next.

coverage.note: Right-handed with the vertical axis up for local frames, usually an Earth-centred Earth-fixed frame at the root, and the frame may be named explicitly through a metadata property carrying a geodetic dataset identifier. Note the up axis differs from the common asset format's.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, clause 6.6 Coordinate reference system
sources.quote: 3D Tiles uses a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system; that is, the cross product of x and y yields z . 3D Tiles defines the z axis as up for local Cartesian coordinate systems.

coverage.note: Fixed at metres, with no way for a tileset to declare anything else. This matches the common asset format and removes one class of scale error.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, clause 6.5 Units
sources.quote: The unit for all linear distances is meters. All angles are in radians.

coverage.note: Point clouds are a named content type in the scope, and the styling language can size individual points and read their position, colour and normal. The dedicated point cloud tile format is deprecated in this version in favour of point primitives in the common asset format. Voxels are not here; they are listed as a feature of the in-development next version.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, clause 1 Scope and clause 10.4 Point Cloud
sources.quote: A Point Cloud is a collection of points that may be styled like other features. In addition to evaluating a point's color and show properties, a Point Cloud style may evaluate pointSize , or the size of each point in pixels.

coverage.note: Every tileset must state the version it targets, and that version fixes both the schema and the permitted tile formats. A second optional field lets a publisher version their own data separately, which is used to defeat caches.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, Annex A.1.1 asset.version
sources.quote: The 3D Tiles version. The version defines the JSON schema for the tileset JSON and the base set of tile formats.

coverage.note: It defines the container for the tree, not for the model. Since this version the model payload is simply the common asset format, and the four original tile formats are deprecated and may be removed. The missing half is a real interoperability cost: an implementation must apply an up-axis correction to every tile, which the specification spells out as a step in the transform chain.

coverage.note: There is a conformance clause, and it is unusually candid about its own limits: conformance is measured against one annex of objects and properties, and the machine-readable schema covers only part of that. There are no conformance classes and no test suite in the document.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1, clause 2 Conformance

coverage.note: A tile carries a four-by-four transform to its parent's frame and the root sits in an Earth-fixed frame, so position and orientation against the Earth are expressible. What is missing is a shared record: this is a matrix in a tileset file, not a portable pose, and the specification never once mentions the pose standard published by the same consortium. Two standards from one body with no link between them is the kind of thing a working group can fix.

A tiled delivery format has no input model and reads nothing about the person looking at it.

Tiles carry renderable content and metadata under bounding volumes, with a subdivision scheme and geometric error to decide what to draw. Nothing in the tileset says which surface is walkable, where the bounds of a body's movement are, or where a visitor arrives — a client that wants to walk a city has to work that out from the geometry.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1
sources.quote: In 3D Tiles, a subset of a tileset containing a reference to renderable content and the metadata, such as the content's bounding volume, which is used by a client to determine if the content is rendered.

coverage.note: A tileset publishes geometry, not units of logic; its declarative styling is expressions evaluated in place, under no published name.
The standard defines how tiles are structured and fetched. It has no publishing service where a review could stand and no field saying what review content has had.

Every tile may carry a 4x4 affine transform that puts its local coordinates into its parent's, and a root tileset is commonly placed in an Earth-centred frame, so a building inside a city inside the Earth all line up. That is alignment inside one tree; the standard declares no map of a place with a version and a lifecycle, and publishes no transform relating its tileset to a second map of the same place.

coverage.note: OGC 3D Tiles is a tiling specification for streaming large 3D geospatial datasets. It defines tilesets, spatial indexing, and level-of-detail for terrain and buildings. It tiles data, not running experiences, and has no containment model.

sources.title: OGC 3D Tiles Specification 1.1
sources.quote: 3D Tiles is designed for streaming and rendering massive 3D geospatial content such as Photogrammetry, 3D Buildings, BIM/CAD, Instanced Features, and Point Clouds.

coverage.note: 3D Tiles is a geospatial tiling standard for streaming large 3D datasets. It has no networking for world state and no mechanism for inter-world coupling.
